title: Reporting chain in a game studio
prompt:
A game studio stores its staff with a manager_id that points to another staff row. Heads of studio have a NULL manager_id, and there can be more than one.

For every person reachable from a head of studio, return their depth and their full reporting chain from the top down, names joined with ' > '. A bad data import left some people in a manager loop with no head above them; leave those out.

- Columns: id, name, depth, chain
- Heads have depth 0 and chain equal to their own name
- Order by depth, then id
- Example chain: 'Ana > Ben > Dee'
hints: You cannot know the number of levels in advance, so a fixed number of self-joins will not do.
Use WITH RECURSIVE: the anchor selects heads (manager_id IS NULL), the recursive part joins staff whose manager is already in the result.
Carry depth + 1 and chain || ' > ' || s.name through the recursion. Starting only from heads means the loop is never entered.

exercise.schema: CREATE TABLE staff (id int PRIMARY KEY, name text NOT NULL, manager_id int REFERENCES staff(id));
exercise.starter:
-- Depth and chain for everyone (only looks one level up)
SELECT s.id, s.name,
  CASE WHEN m.id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS depth,
  coalesce(m.name || ' > ', '') || s.name AS chain
FROM staff s
LEFT JOIN staff m ON m.id = s.manager_id
ORDER BY depth, id;
exercise.solution:
WITH RECURSIVE tree AS (
  SELECT id, name, 0 AS depth, name AS chain
  FROM staff
  WHERE manager_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT s.id, s.name, t.depth + 1, t.chain || ' > ' || s.name
  FROM staff s
  JOIN tree t ON s.manager_id = t.id
)
SELECT id, name, depth, chain
FROM tree
ORDER BY depth, id;

tests.name: two heads of studio
tests.seed: INSERT INTO staff VALUES (1, 'Ana', NULL), (2, 'Bo', NULL), (3, 'Cal', 2);

hiddenTests.name: manager loop is left out
ties on depth order by id not name

explanation: The anchor member selects the heads with depth 0 and their own name as the chain. Each recursive step joins staff rows whose manager_id matches a row found in the previous step, adding 1 to depth and appending the name, so the CTE walks down any number of levels. Because the walk starts only at heads, people in a manager loop are never reached and the query still terminates. The traps are a fixed number of self-joins, which caps the depth, and starting the recursion from every row and walking up, which loops forever on the bad data unless you add a cycle check.
notes: Each recursion step is a join against the working table, so an index on staff(manager_id) keeps deep or wide trees fast. Postgres 14+ supports a CYCLE clause (CYCLE id SET is_cycle USING path) that detects loops when you must start from arbitrary rows. For sorting a whole tree in display order, carry an array of ids as the path and ORDER BY it instead of a text chain.
followUps: Walk upwards from one given employee to the top and detect a loop with the CYCLE clause.
Return each manager's total headcount including indirect reports.
